standard_prerequisites.name: The local Weyl module W((k+1)theta) with its highest weight vector, and the relation (w2) remembering that a sufficiently high power of a negative root vector acts as zero on it
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's section 3, where the module and the relation are set up before the counted statement; the relation is referred to in the proof at source line 367 (a navigation-pointer stub)
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the module in which the two relations hold and supplies the vanishing used at the end of both parts.

standard_prerequisites.name: The commutator of a raising operator with a power of a lowering operator in the current algebra, and the evaluation of the coefficient appearing in the expansion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Computed inside the counted proof at source lines 341-356
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the explicit multiple of the desired vector which equals a vector known to vanish.

standard_prerequisites.name: The commutation relation for two negative root vectors, labelled garland in the article
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof at source line 365 (a navigation-pointer stub)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the second relation after specialising the parameters.

core_obligations: Set up the computation: the proof applies a raising operator to a power of a lowering operator applied to the highest weight vector, and since the raising operator annihilates the highest weight vector it may replace the expression by the commutator (proof lines 341-345)

Expand and substitute: the commutator is expanded as a sum over the intermediate powers, and since the Cartan element annihilates the highest weight vector each term may be replaced by the explicit commutator of that Cartan element with the corresponding power, which is computed (proof lines 346-356)

Conclude part (1): after simplifying, the expression equals an explicit non-zero multiple of the vector appearing in the first relation, and the vanishing of the original expression because a high enough power of the lowering operator kills the highest weight vector gives the relation (proof lines 357-364)

Part (2): the second relation follows by specialising the parameters in the article's labelled commutation relation and using the vanishing of the same high power of the lowering operator (proof lines 365-367)
proof_roadmap: 第 (1) 部分：把 x^+_θ t^{2k+1-i} 作用到 (x^-_θ⊗1)^{2k+3}w 上，因它零化最高权向量可换成交换子；把交换子展开成 j 求和，再用 θ^∨ 零化 w 把每项换成显式交换子 (-2)(2k+3-j)(x^-_θ)^{2k+2-j}(x^-_θ⊗t^{2k+1-i})，化简后等于目标向量的一个非零倍数，而原式因 (x^-_θ)^{2k+3}w = 0 为零。
第 (2) 部分：在文章的交换关系里取 r = 2、s = 2m+1、α = θ，并用 (x^-_θ⊗1)^{2m+3}w = 0（由 (w2)）即得。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement records two relations in the local Weyl module W((k+1)theta): a power of the lowering operator times a twisted vector annihilates the highest weight vector, and a product of two twisted vectors lies in the submodule generated by a higher one (author lemma at source lines 323-338, label g). The proof (source lines 340-368) proves the first relation by a complete commutator computation: it replaces a raising operator applied to a high power of a lowering operator by the commutator, expands it as a sum, substitutes the explicit commutator with the Cartan element, simplifies to a non-zero multiple of the desired vector and uses the vanishing of a high power (proof lines 341-364); the second relation is obtained by specialising the article's labelled commutation relation (proof lines 365-367). The commutator computation is the content. H3.
